title: Injectivity of the sorting position
statement: Let $kf:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $N\in\mathbb N$. For $j<N$, define its sorting position to be the number of indices $m<N$ with $kf(m)<kf(j)$, plus the number of indices $m<j$ with $kf(m)=kf(j)$. If $i,j<N$ have the same sorting position, then $i=j$.
